About Auto King

Auto King is a mobile car repair and inspection business. Its mechanics come to the customer, at home or work, for roadworthy certificates and pre-purchase inspections, and since September for general car repairs.

Google Ads is the main way new customers find them. The campaigns we manage run across Brisbane, the Gold Coast, the Sunshine Coast, Toowoomba, Cairns and Townsville. Most customers are on their phones, so everything we built is designed to be fast and clear on mobile.

  • ServicesRoadworthy · Pre-purchase · Repairs
  • Mobile traffic93%
  • Leads by phone / formAbout 2/3 · 1/3
  • Enquiries that close33–46%
  • Engagement startedMay 2026

May2026Baseline

Auto King’s account looked busy but told us almost nothing: every conversion was worth the same A$1, so return on ad spend read 0.05 and the bidding algorithm had nothing meaningful to learn from.

What we found when we took over

  • Calls only. The only conversion data in the account came from the call extension. No web form submissions were being recorded, even though roughly one in three enquiries arrives by form.
  • Two conversion actions in total. Only “Submit lead form” and “Calls from Call Extension” existed, and neither separated one service from another.
  • Return on spend was effectively zero. 257 conversions carried A$257 of value, a flat A$1 each, so ROAS sat at 0.05. Google could not tell a roadworthy enquiry from a pre-purchase inspection, or an enquiry from a paying customer.

Why that matters

  • Smart Bidding optimises toward whatever conversion signal it is given. With identical values on every conversion it can only chase volume, not revenue.
  • Ads were sending traffic to the general website, where a customer who wanted one specific service had to find their own way.
  • With no form data and no service split, we could not see which campaigns, locations or services were actually earning money.

June2026Foundation

We rebuilt the measurement layer first: service-specific landing pages, a conversion action and tag for every service, and a CRM loop that reports real closed jobs back to Google. ROAS jumped from 0.05 to 1.45.

The foundation: separate what is an enquiry from what is a customer

Three layers of conversion now feed Google Ads, each with a clear role: form fills (secondary, for reporting), valued phone calls (primary), and closed jobs from Monday.com (primary, real revenue).

1. Service-specific PPC landing pages

  • Built in May and live for June: Roadworthy Certificate and Pre-Purchase Inspection. We started with these two services to test the approach before extending it.
  • Why: a visitor who searched for a roadworthy lands on a page about roadworthies only. No full-site menu to wander through, so they call or fill the form straight away. With 93% of traffic on mobile, a short focused page converts better than a busy homepage.
  • Location in the page. Each page reads the campaign’s location and shows it at the top, so someone searching in Cairns sees Cairns. It feels made for them, which lifts trust and conversion.
  • GCLID in the form. A hidden field stores the Google Click ID with every enquiry. Without it, a job closed weeks later cannot be traced to the ad click that produced it.

2. Conversion actions and GTM tags, one set per service

  • Created separate conversion actions and Google Tag Manager tags for Roadworthy and Pre-Purchase. Google can now see which service generated each conversion, which is what makes service-level optimisation possible.
  • Form fills → Secondary, with a value per service. A form fill is an enquiry, not a sale, and only a minority of enquiries turn into jobs. Keeping them secondary means they report in the account without teaching the algorithm that every enquiry is a customer.
  • Phone calls → Primary, with a value. Calls are the highest-intent action and about two-thirds of all leads. Calls from ads and tap-to-call taps were set up as primary, valued actions so bidding is steered toward callers. (Calls placed from the landing pages themselves were added as their own actions in September, see below.)

3. Monday.com: closing the loop on real customers

  • Monday.com is the CRM where every lead is logged and tracked through to a booked job. When a lead is marked as won, that job and its value are sent back to Google Ads against the original click (via the GCLID).
  • We created “Closed Job” conversion actions per service (Roadworthy, Pre-Purchase, and later Diagnostics, Servicing and Repairs) and set them to Primary. Google now sees paying customers, not just enquiries, and can find more people like them.
  • First imports arrived in June: 9 Roadworthy closed jobs (A$1,181) and 3 Pre-Purchase closed jobs (A$427).

4. Campaign optimisation

  • Created new, more relevant location campaigns and refreshed ad copy to match the service pages.
  • Introduced ad scheduling and moved to bidding strategies suited to the new value signals.

What we did

  • Keyword research turned into search themes. Researched what customers actually type when they need a roadworthy or an inspection, then added those phrases as search themes so Performance Max leans toward real demand.
  • Audience research and audience signals. Researched the audience behind Auto King’s customers, then built audience signals to point the algorithm at similar people from day one.
  • Negative keywords. Built negative keyword lists from search-term data to keep spend off irrelevant searches.
  • Landing pages updated with what we learned. Adjusted headlines, proof points and calls to action on the service pages to reflect the trends and objections seen in the data.
  • Insight analysis, campaign by campaign. Reviewed performance by location and service each week and adjusted campaigns accordingly.

What the data showed

  • ROAS more than doubled in a month, from 1.45 to 3.40, on conversion value of A$26,646 against A$7,836 of cost.
  • Average CPC fell from A$2.84 to A$2.43 while impressions grew by 27,907, so we paid less per click on a larger audience.
  • Closed jobs scaled: 126 Roadworthy jobs (A$17,147) and 8 Pre-Purchase jobs (A$1,328) were imported into Google Ads.
  • Strongest campaigns by ROAS: Townsville (7.23), Cairns (5.27) and Sunshine Coast South (5.13). Weakest: Gold Coast North (2.25) and Sunshine Coast North (2.24).

Optimisation focus

  • Campaign-level return review. Ranked every location campaign by ROAS and cost per conversion. Townsville, Sunshine Coast North and the three Brisbane campaigns lead; Gold Coast North, Gold Coast South and Sunshine Coast South lag.
  • Budget follows return. Four campaigns (Brisbane North, West, South and Gold Coast North) were still limited by budget, so spend priority was weighed against ROAS rather than split evenly.
  • Fixing the weak spots. For the lowest-return campaigns we tightened search themes and negatives, and aligned asset group copy and the landing page more closely to the searcher’s service and location.
  • Ongoing search-term review. Continued weekly search-term checks to remove wasted clicks and surface new phrases worth targeting.

What the data showed

  • Efficiency up while spend fell: cost dropped from A$7,836 to A$6,814 and ROAS rose to 3.68.
  • Sunshine Coast North recovered: ROAS rose from 2.24 in July to 5.51 in August. Gold Coast North (2.35) and Gold Coast South (1.77) remain the priority.
  • Real revenue dominates the signal. 150 Roadworthy closed jobs (A$20,170) and 4 Pre-Purchase closed jobs (A$716) now carry most of the conversion value Google sees.
  • Form fills kept growing: 394 Roadworthy form fills (A$20,488) and 20 Pre-Purchase form fills (A$1,200) were recorded as secondary actions for reporting.
  • Average CPC rose to A$2.84 from A$2.43, an area we are watching as we scale into stronger auctions.

Optimisation: every call tracked, attributed to its service

Calls are about two-thirds of Auto King’s leads, so we extended call measurement in stages. Stage one (May–June) fixed the biggest distortion: flat A$1 values and no CRM feedback. Stage two, in September, added dedicated “Calls from Website” conversion actions for each service, so calls made from the landing pages are recorded alongside calls made from the ads.

Each service has its own action (Roadworthy, Pre-Purchase, Car Repairs), so Google and our reporting can see which service, campaign and page produced each call. In September this tracked 41 Roadworthy calls (A$1,640) and 2 Pre-Purchase calls (A$80) from the landing pages, on top of 45 calls from ad call extensions (A$2,925). The Car Repairs call action is live and waiting for its first calls.

Brand campaign

  • Search-term research showed a large volume of people searching for Auto King by name. Those searches are the cheapest, highest-intent traffic the business can get, and they are also open to competitors bidding on the Auto King name.
  • We built a dedicated brand Search campaign using Target Impression Share bidding, so Auto King holds a top position whenever someone searches for it. That protects our impression share on brand terms, stops competitors taking those clicks, and keeps brand spend and results separate from the prospecting campaigns so neither distorts the other.
  • A dedicated brand landing page carries this traffic, with its own conversion tags so brand leads are measured on their own.
  • First results: 63 conversions at A$13.81 each, a 29.3% conversion rate, and 10 brand closed jobs worth A$1,490 already imported from Monday.com.

Dedicated Pre-Purchase campaign

  • Pre-Purchase is the higher-value service, so it now has its own Brisbane Performance Max campaign with its own budget and bidding, rather than sharing with roadworthies.
  • First days of delivery: 153 clicks and 6.5 conversions.

Monitoring scripts

  • Added Google Ads scripts that watch conversion volume and campaign activity and send an immediate email alert if conversions drop, a campaign stops delivering, or something else breaks.
  • Why: Smart Bidding is only as good as its tracking. If a GTM tag fails or a campaign stalls, results can slide for weeks before anyone notices. The alerts mean we catch it within hours, fix it, and keep the conversion data clean.

New service: Mechanics (car repairs)

  • At the client’s request we launched car repairs. We built a dedicated Car Repairs landing page and followed the same blueprint as the first two services.
  • Added GTM tags (thank-you trigger, Google Ads conversion, GA4 event and tap-to-call), plus conversion actions for form fill, calls and Closed Job.
  • Added a new Car Repairs asset group inside each location campaign, so the service is promoted everywhere we already advertise.
  • First results: 5 Car Repairs form fills (A$620) and 3 Car Repairs closed jobs (A$447) in September.

What the data showed (1–15 October)

  • Best return and best efficiency yet: ROAS 4.12 and A$22.40 per conversion, with 234 conversions in half a month against 305 for all of September.
  • More of the clicks convert. Conversion rate rose to 12.29% from 9.69%. Average CPC is higher at A$3.57 (Sept: A$2.57), so we are paying more per click for clicks that convert better.
  • Dedicated Pre-Purchase campaign is the standout: ROAS 8.04 and A$15.06 per conversion, turning A$444 of spend into A$3,571 of value. Pre-Purchase closed jobs reached 9 (A$2,392) in 15 days, against 4 (A$716) in all of September.
  • Brand campaign: 41 conversions at A$11.17, ROAS 5.36, 50 phone calls and 7 closed jobs (A$1,063). Impression share lost to budget fell from 69% to 35%.
  • Call tracking is capturing the volume: 143 calls recorded from the website actions (39 main site, 101 Roadworthy, 3 Pre-Purchase) plus 2 from ad call extensions, 146 in total. September’s full month recorded 98.
  • Mechanics is building: 16 Car Repairs form fills (A$1,984) and 4 Car Repairs closed jobs (A$676).

Optimisation focus

  • Scale what is proven. The dedicated Pre-Purchase campaign is now the template: its own budget and bidding for the higher-value service, rather than sharing with roadworthies.
  • Brand budget headroom. Brand searches were losing 69% of impression share to budget in September; that is now 35%, so Auto King appears more often when people search for it by name.
  • Competitor campaign launched 13 October. First signals: 129 impressions, 11 clicks and 1 conversion worth A$149. Delivery is limited by its bid strategy, so we are monitoring it closely before changing anything.
  • Every call carries a value. The main-site number now records valued calls (39, A$1,840) alongside the service-specific actions, so Smart Bidding weighs calls as revenue, not just activity.
  • Fix before funding. Gold Coast North (ROAS 1.32) is limited by budget but returns the least, so landing page and asset group improvements come before any extra budget.
  • Safeguards stay on. The conversion-drop and campaign alerts keep running, and weekly search-term reviews continue to trim wasted clicks.
